5 easy ways to reuse your old monitor

By  Saeed Wazir
Published Nov 19, 2026, 2:00 AM EST

Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents:
Try something different:

Monitors are usually durable and will probably last longer than your PC. However, they’ll still eventually need upgrading to newer models with larger screens or higher resolution for watching content. The question is what to do with your old monitor after you've bought a new one.

Add Pocket-lint on Google Add as Preferred Source

Smartphones are more versatile and easier to reuse for other purposes than monitors, which are mainly for graphics and don't have other uses. However, you can still plug other devices into your monitor's USB or HDMI ports and reuse them for tasks other than being connected to your PC. Here are five ways I reuse my old monitors after I've upgraded to a new one.

Turn them into a desktop PC

A cheap mini PC

I often use my old monitors as desktop PCs by connecting them to my Galaxy phone via Samsung DeX. The process is simple: I plug my phone into the monitor’s HDMI port with a compatible cable. I then connect my mouse and keyboard, and I'm ready to go. My phone becomes a PC with capabilities similar to my laptop.

This isn't the most imaginative way to repurpose your monitor, but it can give it a new life.

This works on full-size models, but I often prefer using portable monitors. I don't need to lug my bulky laptop around; I can just use my phone and monitor when I'm on the go. This isn't the most imaginative way to repurpose your monitor, but it can give it a new life, and is especially worth it for those who don't have a desktop to use it with.

Smart home display

Cheap and easy

Turning an old monitor into a smart home display makes sense and can save you money. It's straightforward, but you'll need to pair it with an old phone, Raspberry Pi, or an old PC.

Turning an old monitor into a smart home display makes sense and can save you money.

Then download the DAKboard app onto your device and plug it into the monitor. The app is user-friendly and offers many preset themes. You can also use the manual wizard if you prefer a custom display. After you're done, you'll have a smart home monitor that shows a calendar, the weather, events happening this week, and whatever else you want to see.

Smart TV

Some hardware required

Turning your monitor into a smart TV is one of the easiest and cheapest ways to reuse it. All you need to do is buy an Amazon Fire Stick, Roku, or Google TV Stick and plug it into the monitor's HDMI port.

Monitors typically don't have built-in speakers, so you'll need to add some to hear the audio.

Monitors typically don't have built-in speakers, so you'll need to add some to hear the audio. They usually don't have Bluetooth, HDMI ARC, or eARC ports either, so you'll need to connect your speakers via the 3.5mm audio port. If your monitor doesn't have one, you can try getting a USB audio adapter that plugs into your monitor and includes a 3.5mm jack.

CCTV monitor

Improve your safety

You can always connect your old monitor to your DVR and use it to monitor your CCTV cameras. Yes, it's not a groundbreaking idea, but it can save you money and improve your safety to prevent harm to your family.

I like having a CCTV display in my bedroom to check outside noises at night. I also like having one in the lounge or dining room, so everyone can see who's at my gate. Old monitors are capable, and all I do is plug them into the DVR via HDMI. My DVR has a single HDMI port, so I used a splitter and ran a long HDMI cable through the ceiling to the other room.

Make it a secondary or tertiary monitor

You can never have enough screen space

Why get rid of your old monitor when you can keep it and expand your setup? You can never have enough screen space and double or triple monitor setups boost your efficiency and give you amazing flexibility. For example, you can have a YouTube video playing on the first monitor, multiple browser tabs on the second, and the document or email you're typing on the third.

Connecting two or even three monitors is simple in Windows provided your PC and monitors have compatible USB-C or HDMI ports.

Connecting two or even three monitors is simple in Windows provided your PC and monitors have compatible USB-C or HDMI ports. Even if they don't, you can always buy an adapter to get them to work. Then you just plug them in to the ports and they should be detected automatically. Then you right-click on your desktop, click on Display, and select Extend these displays.
